description: This file defines classes and functions related to benchmarking and timing PyTorch code, including a Timer class that extends the timeit.Timer with PyTorch-specific features. It includes support for CPU and CUDA accelerators, C++ timing via JIT compilation, and methods for collecting detailed performance metrics like instruction counts.

classes.description: Enum representing the programming language context (Python or C++) for timing.

classes.name: CPPTimer
classes.description: Class for timing C++ code snippets with global setup and statement, utilizing JIT compilation.

classes.name: Timer
classes.description: Main class that extends timeit.Timer with PyTorch-aware features including accelerator synchronization, warmup, multiple measurement strategies, and callgrind instruction counting.

methods.name: float timer()
methods.description: Function that returns the current time, synchronized with PyTorch accelerators if available.

methods.name: TimeitTimer.timeit
methods.description: Executes the statement a given number of times and returns the total time, with PyTorch-specific adjustments in Timer.

methods.name: Timer.timeit
methods.description: Measures execution time of the statement, returning a Measurement object with timing details.

methods.name: Timer.blocked_autorange
methods.description: Measures multiple replicates using block sizing to minimize overhead, returning a Measurement.

methods.name: Timer.adaptive_autorange
methods.description: Measures until a specified confidence threshold is met or maximum time is reached, returning a Measurement.

methods.name: Timer.collect_callgrind
methods.description: Runs the statement under Callgrind to collect instruction counts for performance analysis.
